Putuo Mountain

普陀山 - Sacred Buddhist Island in the East China Sea

Overview

Putuo Mountain (Putuoshan) is one of China's four sacred Buddhist mountains, located on a small island in the Zhoushan Archipelago off the coast of Zhejiang Province. Dedicated to Guanyin (the Goddess of Mercy), Putuo has been a major Buddhist pilgrimage site for over 1,000 years. The island features stunning coastal scenery with ancient temples perched on rocky cliffs, golden-roofed monastery complexes, pristine beaches, and lush forests. The largest temple, Puji Temple, is a magnificent complex of halls and courtyards. Putuo combines spiritual significance with natural beauty — dramatic sea cliffs, sandy beaches, and crystal-clear waters make it a unique destination among China's sacred mountains.

Quick Facts

  • Location: Zhoushan Islands, Zhejiang Province
  • UNESCO Status: Part of "Mount Putuo" cultural landscape
  • Island Area: 12.5 square kilometers
  • Best Time to Visit: April-June, September-November (mild weather)
  • Entrance Fee: ¥160 (island entry) + individual temple fees (¥5-10 each)
  • Opening Hours: 6:30 AM - 9:30 PM (ferry hours vary)

How to Get There - Transportation

Ferry from Shanghai

From Shanghai: Bus to Shenjiawan Dock (2.5h, ¥50), then ferry to Putuo (1.5h, ¥100-130). Or direct ferry from Shanghai Wusongkou (4h, ¥150-200). Most popular route for tourists.

Ferry from Ningbo

From Ningbo: Bus to Zhujiajian Dock (1.5h, ¥30), then ferry to Putuo (15 min, ¥30). Fastest route. High-speed ferry available (¥50, 10 min).

By Air to Zhoushan

Zhoushan Putuoshan Airport: Flights from Beijing, Shanghai, Guangzhou. Airport to dock: taxi 20 min (¥50). Then ferry to island (15 min).

On the Island

Walking & Bus: Island is small and walkable. Tourist buses connect major temples (¥5-10 per ride). No private cars allowed. Bicycles available for rent.

Recommended Tour Routes

Route 1: Classic One-Day Pilgrimage

Route: Puji Temple → Fayu Temple → Huiji Temple (cable car) → Nanhai Guanyin Statue → Beach
Duration: 6-8 hours
Best for: First-time visitors, pilgrims

Route 2: Two-Day Spiritual Retreat

Day 1: Puji Temple → Fayu Temple → Evening chanting at temple
Day 2: Huiji Temple (sunrise) → Guanyin Statue → Rocky coast walk → Departure
Best for: Deep spiritual experience

Route 3: Scenic & Cultural Tour

Focus: Coastal scenery + temples + beach
Highlights: Thousand-Step Beach, Purple Bamboo Forest, Chaoyin Cave, Guanyin Statue
Duration: 1-2 days

Route 4: Photography & Nature

Best Spots: Sunrise from Huiji Temple, Coastal cliffs, Stone bridge, Beach at sunset
Tips: Early morning for misty temple atmosphere; golden hour for coastal shots

Essential Travel Tips

  • Best Season: April-June and September-November for mild weather. Summer (Jul-Aug) is hot and crowded. Winter is quiet but cold and windy.
  • Ferry Schedule: Ferries run from 6:30 AM to 9:30 PM (varies by season). Check schedule before planning. Last ferry back is important — don't miss it!
  • Temple Etiquette: Dress modestly (cover shoulders and knees). Remove hats inside temples. Don't point fingers at Buddha statues. Photography may be restricted inside halls.
  • Buddhist Holidays: Guanyin's birthday (19th day of 2nd, 6th, and 9th lunar months) draws huge crowds. Avoid if you prefer quiet.
  • Vegetarian Food: Temple vegetarian meals are a unique experience. Available at lunch only (10:30 AM - 1 PM). Very affordable and delicious.
  • Cable Car: Available to Huiji Temple (top of mountain). ¥40 one way. Saves 45 min of steep climbing.
  • Crowds: Weekends and holidays are extremely crowded. Weekdays are much quieter. Early morning (before 8 AM) is most peaceful.
  • Beach: Thousand-Step Beach is the main swimming beach. Clean and well-maintained. Entrance ¥20.
  • Weather: Island weather can change quickly. Bring rain gear. Typhoon season (Jul-Sep) may cancel ferries.
  • Payment: WeChat Pay and Alipay accepted everywhere. ATMs available near ferry dock and main temple area.
